scope: src/campaignStoryExperience.js, src/campaignRoomFlows.js, src/campaign/nativeEncounterNarrative.js, src/campaign/nativeEncounterTactics.js, src/campaignObjectives.js, src/campaignFloorplanAuthoring.js (campaign/story structure, room flows, objectives, native encounter narrative/tactics). Cross-referenced src/main.js, src/encounterDirector.js, src/encounterBehavior.js, src/campaignEncounters.js for wiring.

findings.title: campaignCuePack only defines a 'pressure' setpiece, but no building ever sets setpiece.kind='pressure' — buildings 4-12 get zero setpiece story cues
findings.description: campaignCuePack (used for buildings 4-12) authors setpieces.pressure ({start,trigger,silenced}). updateStoryExperience looks up cues.setpieces[setpiece.kind] (line 404). SETPIECE_DEFS in main.js (lines 36025-36034) only ever sets kind to 'alarm'|'hostage'|'ambush'|'sniper'|'dark'|'survival' — never 'pressure'. So for buildings 4-8 (which DO run real setpieces: sniper/dark/survival/ambush/alarm), cues.setpieces[kind] is undefined, cset is undefined, cloneCue(undefined) returns null, and no SETPIECE_LIVE / REINFORCEMENTS / PRESSURE-BROKEN story cue ever shows. The hand-written 'pressure' cue block is dead for every building. Buildings 1-3 are fine because they author the matching kind keys (alarm/hostage/ambush).
findings.evidence: campaignStoryExperience.js setpieces.pressure block (lines 30-36) keyed 'pressure'; updateStoryExperience line 404: `const cset = cues.setpieces && cues.setpieces[kind];`. main.js SETPIECE_DEFS 4:{type:'sniper'},5:{type:'dark'},6:{type:'survival'},7:{type:'ambush'},8:{type:'alarm'} — grep for kind:'pressure'/type:'pressure' returns nothing in main.js.
findings.fix: In campaignCuePack, key the setpiece pack by the actual kind each building uses instead of the generic 'pressure'. Simplest robust fix: change the lookup in updateStoryExperience line 404 to fall back to a generic pack, e.g. `const cset = (cues.setpieces && (cues.setpieces[kind] || cues.setpieces.pressure)) || null;` so the authored 'pressure' copy is reused for any unmapped kind. Buildings 4-8 then surface their setpiece cues. Keeps story-experience-static-probe green (it only asserts B1-3).
findings.risk: Low. Additive; only affects buildings whose setpiece cue is currently absent. No save-compat impact (cues are transient). Verify the generic 'pressure' copy reads acceptably for sniper/dark/survival kinds.

findings.title: Hand-authored COVER_HINT_ANCHOR_PATCH_BY_BN values for buildings 2-7 and 10 are silently overwritten at module load by the computed loop
findings.description: COVER_HINT_ANCHOR_PATCH_BY_BN is hand-authored at lines 7-55 with tuned per-building anchors (e.g. B2 relay_desk:[-13.9,2.45], drum_spool:[14.35,0.12], spine_pinch:[0.35,2.25]). The module-load loop at 167-199 does `COVER_HINT_ANCHOR_PATCH_BY_BN[bn] = { ...(existing||{}), <computed> }`, and the computed object always re-sets the SAME keys (spine_pinch, relay_desk, drum_spool, intake_apron, west_lane_fork, east_stack, fe_stack, cage_pillar_west, cage_center_low, vestibule_face, desk_rail). Because computed keys come AFTER the spread, they win. Verified: every hand-authored anchor for B2,B3,B4,B5,B6,B7,B10 is overwritten (0 survive); B8,B9,B11,B12 use distinct names (rack_face/cold_row/customs_lane/etc) that survive but aren't in the computed set. These anchors are consumed live by _resolveCoverAnchor in encounterBehavior.js (line 162-164) to bias enemy cover selection, so the designer's manual tuning is discarded and replaced by route-center approximations that can differ by several meters (B2 relay_desk: authored [-13.9,2.45] vs computed objective_preview center ~[-7.15,-1.0]).
findings.evidence: Lines 176-190 set spine_pinch/relay_desk/drum_spool/etc unconditionally; line 176 spreads existing first: `COVER_HINT_ANCHOR_PATCH_BY_BN[bn] = { ...(COVER_HINT_ANCHOR_PATCH_BY_BN[bn] || {}), intake_apron: ..., ... relay_desk: objective || [-14,2], ... }`. Only the `if (bn===1)` block (191-198) re-pins values after; bn 2-12 keep computed. encounterBehavior.js:163 `if (patch && patch[hint]) return patch[hint];`.
findings.fix: Invert the merge so hand-authored values take precedence: build the computed defaults first, then spread the authored map on top, e.g. `COVER_HINT_ANCHOR_PATCH_BY_BN[bn] = { <computed defaults>, ...(authored[bn] || {}) };` (capture the original authored map into a const before the loop so the spread isn't reading the already-mutated object). This preserves the tuned B2-B10 anchors and still fills gaps with route-derived fallbacks.
findings.risk: Low-medium. Changes enemy cover bias positions back to the authored intent for B2-B10 (a behavior change vs current shipped values). Confirm authored anchors are still inside valid room bounds. No save-compat / no build-graph impact; validate-campaign / validate-room-flow do not check these.

findings.title: Alarm setpiece shows the same 'Alarm Silenced' cue twice (silenced + reward paths reuse cset.silenced with different keys)
findings.description: For the alarm setpiece (B01), when the player silences the relay and clears zone 1, SETPIECE._relaySilenced and SETPIECE.rewardGiven both become true. The 'silenced' branch (lines 422-426) enqueues cset.silenced with key `setpiece:1:alarm:silenced`; the 'rewardGiven' branch (lines 427-430) enqueues the SAME cset.silenced object with key `setpiece:1:alarm:reward`. Different keys defeat the seen-dedup, so the identical 'PRESSURE/RELAY SAFE — Alarm Silenced' banner displays twice back-to-back.
findings.evidence: Line 425 `enqueueCue(s, cloneCue(cset && cset.silenced, {...}), `setpiece:${building}:${kind}:silenced`);` and line 429 `enqueueCue(s, cloneCue(cset && cset.silenced, {...}), `setpiece:${building}:${kind}:reward`);` — both reference cset.silenced.
findings.fix: Either drop the reward-path enqueue (lines 427-430) since 'silenced' already covers the success message, or give the reward branch a distinct cue (e.g. a payout/clear cue) instead of reusing cset.silenced. Minimal: gate the reward enqueue with `if (!s.lastSetpieceSilenced)` so it only fires when silenced didn't already.
findings.risk: Very low. Removes a redundant banner. No state-shape change.

findings.title: B02/B03 boss reveal cues omit tone/duration args, rendering with tone='story' (3300ms) instead of 'boss' (3800ms)
findings.description: The boss cues for B01 (line 75) and the campaignCuePack default (line 40) pass tone='boss', durationMs=3800. But B02 (line 107) and B03 (line 139) call cue('boss','TARGET LINE', title, body) with no tone/duration, so they default to tone='story' and durationMs=3300. _renderStoryExperienceCue sets root.dataset.tone=cue.tone (main.js line 34361), which drives the boss-colored styling. So the dramatic boss-reveal banner on Continental Lobby and Club Obsidian is styled as a plain 'story' cue and shown for a shorter time than every other building's boss reveal — a visible inconsistency at the climax moment of two of the first three levels.
findings.evidence: Line 75: `boss: cue('boss','TARGET LINE','Foreman Guard Exposed','...','boss',3800)`. Line 107: `boss: cue('boss','TARGET LINE','Manager Suite Exposed','The bagman is behind the guard line. Clear the suite.')` — no tone/duration. Line 139 same pattern for B03.
findings.fix: Add `, 'boss', 3800` to the cue() calls at lines 107 and 139 to match B01 and the campaignCuePack default.
findings.risk: Trivial. Pure data fix; matches existing buildings. No probe asserts these.

findings.title: Hostage 'discipline broken' cue uses a fixed dedup key so only the first hostage hit ever surfaces a cue
findings.description: On a hostage hit, progress increments (main.js setpieceCheckHostageHit, line 36230). updateStoryExperience enqueues cset.trigger with the constant key `setpiece:${building}:hostage:hostage-hit` (line 419). After the first hit the seen-map suppresses all subsequent hostage-hit cues, so hitting a 2nd/3rd civilian produces no further story feedback even though each is a fresh mastery failure. May be intended (single warning), but it contradicts the per-hit progress comparison `progress > s.lastSetpieceProgress` which implies per-event firing.
findings.evidence: Line 418 `if (kind === 'hostage' && progress > s.lastSetpieceProgress)` then line 419 enqueues with fixed key `:hostage-hit`. The progress guard re-arms each hit but the constant key blocks re-enqueue.
findings.fix: If per-hit feedback is desired, fold progress into the key: `setpiece:${building}:${kind}:hostage-hit:${progress}`. If a single warning is intended, drop the misleading `progress > lastSetpieceProgress` comparison and document it.
findings.risk: Very low. Only affects repeat-hostage-hit feedback in B02. No state-shape change.

findings.title: traverse_objective and objective trigger branches execute identical code (duplicate branch)
findings.description: In the director-trigger handling, `trigger.type === 'traverse_objective'` (378-380) and `trigger.type === 'objective'` (381-383) run byte-identical bodies: completeTextForObjective + enqueue with the same key shape. Both director trigger types are real (encounterDirector emits 'traverse_objective' at line 739 and 'objective' at line 861), so this isn't unreachable, but the two branches are redundant and could collapse to one condition. Minor maintainability/contradiction smell, not a runtime bug.
findings.evidence: Lines 378-383: `} else if (trigger.type === 'traverse_objective') { const c = completeTextForObjective(cues, trigger.id); enqueueCue(...:complete`); } else if (trigger.type === 'objective') { const c = completeTextForObjective(cues, trigger.id); enqueueCue(...:complete`); }` — identical.

findings.title: Alarm reinforcement entry alternates FE/FW per building, but the spawn toast always says 'East flank response incoming'
findings.description: mergeNativeEncounterTactics sets r.entry = bn%2===0 ? 'spawnDoor_FE' : 'spawnDoor_FW' so reinforcements alternate east/west door per building. _spawnB01AlarmReinforcements (main.js line 35167-35169) correctly picks the west door for FW and east for FE. But the on-screen toast (main.js line 35196) is hardcoded to 'East flank response incoming' regardless of entry. For odd buildings (FW = west door) the enemies enter from the west while the banner claims east, contradicting the visible spawn direction.
findings.evidence: nativeEncounterTactics.js line 309 `const entryAlt = bn % 2 === 0 ? 'spawnDoor_FE' : 'spawnDoor_FW';`. main.js line 35196 `attachToast('...East flank response incoming',2500);` is unconditional. The entry token is honored for door selection (35167-35169) but not for the toast copy.
findings.fix: In _spawnB01AlarmReinforcements (main.js ~35196) derive the side from the resolved `door`/`entry` and word the toast accordingly (e.g. west vs east). Alternatively keep the alternation but make the entry default deterministic so the toast stays truthful. (Toast line itself is in main.js, outside this module, but the contradiction originates in the tactics module setting the alternation.)
findings.risk: Very low. Copy-only change in main.js; no logic/state impact.

findings.title: Rich per-cue 'tone' metadata (danger/boss/success/objective) is authored but only mapped to a data-attribute — high-value, low-risk styling hook
findings.description: Every cue carries a semantic tone ('story','danger','objective','success','boss'). The renderer only forwards it as root.dataset.tone (main.js 34361). This is a cheap, immediately-visible AAA opportunity: tone-driven accent color, icon, and a brief impact flash/shake on 'danger'/'boss' cues would make reinforcement warnings and boss reveals read like a AAA mission banner the moment they appear, at near-zero risk because the data already exists and is plumbed through. (Styling lives in src/styles/game.css, outside scope, but the data contract that enables it is here.)
findings.evidence: cue() factory (lines 5-6) stores tone; danger cues at lines 32-34/38/68/73/100/105/132/137, boss at 40/75, success at 27/34/41 etc. main.js 34361 `root.dataset.tone=cue.tone||'story';` is the only consumer.
findings.fix: In src/styles/game.css add `#story-cue[data-tone="danger"]`, `[data-tone="boss"]`, `[data-tone="success"]` accent rules (left-border color, tag color) plus a one-shot keyframe flash on those tones; reuse the existing storyCueIn keyframe. No JS change needed — the tone is already on the element.
findings.risk: Low. CSS-only; falls back to current look if a tone is missing. Confirm contrast/a11y.
